title: Map Scale Calculator: Ground Distance
description: Turn a map measurement into ground distance with the Map Scale Calculator — enter a scale like 1:50,000 and read metres, km and miles. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, on a 1:50,000 hiking map, 5 cm between two points is 2.50 km (1.55 miles) of real ground — the conversion every paper-map walker does with a ruler.
quick_answer: The Map Scale Calculator converts a distance measured on a map into the distance on the ground. Enter the map's scale, such as 1:50,000, and your measured centimetres, and it returns ground metres, kilometres and miles — the arithmetic of maps, done without the slip that ruins a walk plan.

body.t: The 1:25,000 and 1:50,000 sheets still rule British and European hiking. Measuring a leg and converting it here turns 'about two centimetres' into a time estimate you can plan lunch around.
Scale conversion is a set-piece skill. Checking a hand calculation against this tool separates method errors from ruler errors before the exam does it for real.
Site plans, planning applications and estate drawings all carry scales. A measured line on the printout becomes a defensible ground figure with this calculator.

At 1:50,000, one centimetre is 500 m of ground. A ridge line measuring 7.4 cm is therefore 3.70 km (2.30 mi) — before the path's bends, which a paper measurement always undercounts slightly.

At 1:25,000, one centimetre is 250 m, so a 10 cm map distance is exactly 2.50 km. The same walk covers twice the paper on the more detailed sheet — which is the entire trade the scale number describes.

popular_table.title: Common map scales
popular_table.intro: What one measured centimetre (and a typical 5 cm leg) means on the ground at the scales walkers and planners meet most. Pure ratio arithmetic.
popular_table.note: Scales are ratios, unit-free: 1:50,000 means one of anything on the map stands for 50,000 of the same on the ground.

faq: One unit on the map represents 50,000 of the same unit on the ground: 1 cm = 50,000 cm = 500 m. The second number is the denominator you enter in this calculator.

On a single hiking sheet, barely — topographic maps are drawn to keep local scale honest. Across a whole atlas page at small scales, the printed scale is nominal and varies by latitude; treat such conversions as approx.
My map has no printed scale, only a scale bar. Can I still work?
Yes — measure a known ground distance (or the scale bar itself) to recover the ratio, then use this calculator with that denominator.
What if I photocopied or resized the map?
The printed scale is then wrong. Recover the effective scale from a feature of known length before converting anything else.
The ratio does not care, as long as both sides use the same unit. This calculator takes centimetres, the convention on metric topographic series.
Is a bigger denominator a bigger scale?
Opposite: 1:25,000 is a larger scale (more detail, less area) than 1:250,000. The fraction is the scale — bigger fraction, bigger scale.
Can it convert ground distance back to map distance?
Yes — divide the ground distance by the denominator. The sibling Map Scale Ground Distance Calculator is organised around that direction.
